**Synopsis:**
Heading into the Fed's July 28-29 meeting under new Chairman Kevin Warsh, rate futures price roughly a 1-in-3 chance of a 25bps hike — but most economists see the bar as higher than that implies. Inflation has cooled modestly (CPI 3.5%, core 2.6%), a US-Iran ceasefire temporarily eased energy prices (now reversing), and the labor market remains solid. The central debate is not whether the Fed hikes this week, but whether it is ready to commit to a full hiking cycle — historically the Fed rarely does a one-and-done. September is the base-case for the first hike (Capital Economics, BofA), with Wrightson ICAP as a dissenting voice favoring a July move. At least 1-3 dissents are expected Wednesday regardless.
